game.description: A coin is picked at random from a set of coins: P(heads) = 0.5 with probability 1/2, P(heads) = 1 with probability 1/2. The coin is not shown. It is flipped 6 times. Revealed flips show 1 for heads and 0 for tails.
game.contract: The contract settles at the number of heads in all flips.

info.raw:
Settlement value distribution:
- With probability 1/2 the coin is fair, so the value is Binomial(6, 0.5) with mean 3.
- With probability 1/2 the coin always lands heads, so the value is 6.
- The expected value is 4.5. The value is 6 with probability about 0.508.

**Ask side**
- An informed trader buys at my ask only if the true value is strictly above it.
- At an ask of 6.0 that never happens, so informed traders cannot hurt me on this side.
- Noise traders still buy about 19% of the time, for an edge of 1.5. That gives an expected profit of about 0.18 per quote, which is the best ask I found.

**Bid side**
- A bid of 2.8 balances noise-trader edge against informed selling when the value is 0, 1 or 2.
- Noise traders sell about 16% of the time, for an edge of 1.7, which contributes about 0.176.
- Informed selling costs about 0.07.
- The net is about 0.106, roughly the best among the bids I tried.

{"bid": 2.8, "ask": 6.0}

Prior: the coin is fair with probability 1/2, giving a mean of 3 heads. Otherwise it is double-headed, giving 6 heads. So the expected settlement is 4.5. P(V=6) ≈ 0.508, and below 6 the values are spread binomially.

**Ask side:** Any ask below 6 loses to informed traders about 51% of the time, when V=6. I checked expected profit per quote for several asks:

| Ask | Expected profit |
|---|---|
| 5.0 | ≈ −0.05 |
| 5.5 | ≈ +0.09 |
| 5.9 | ≈ +0.17 |
| 6.0 | ≈ +0.18 |
| 6.2 | ≈ +0.18 |

At 6.0 informed traders never buy, so 6.0 is about optimal.

**Bid side:** I made the same check for the bid:

| Bid | Expected profit |
|---|---|
| 2.5 | ≈ +0.104 |
| 2.8 | ≈ +0.106 |
| 3.0 | ≈ +0.10 |
| 3.5 | ≈ +0.04 |

So a bid of about 2.8 is best. The no-trade on quote 1 tells us little, so I keep the same quote.

{"bid": 2.8, "ask": 6.0}

The first flip came up tails, so the coin must be the fair one. That leaves a value of 1 + Binomial(4, 0.5): the mean is 3, and the outcomes 1 to 5 have probabilities 1/16, 4/16, 6/16, 4/16 and 1/16.

**Ask side.** I sell at ask a, and my expected profit is:

0.35·E[(a−V)·1{V>a}] + 0.65·(a−3)·P(noise valuation > a)

The first term is the loss to informed traders, who buy only when the value beats my ask. The second is the gain from noise traders, whose valuations are 3 plus Normal noise with standard deviation 1.7.

| Ask | Expected profit |
|---|---|
| 3.5 | ≈ 0.05 |
| 4.0 | ≈ 0.16 |
| 4.5 | ≈ 0.17 |
| 4.7 | ≈ 0.17 |

An ask around 4.5 is the best of these.

**Bid side.** The problem is symmetric around 3, so the bid should be about 1.5.

{"bid": 1.5, "ask": 4.5}

Flip 1 was tails, so the coin must be the fair one. The settlement value is therefore 1 plus a Binomial(4, 0.5) draw. Before any trading that has a mean of 3, with possible values from 1 to 5.

**Updating on the last trade.** Someone bought at 4.5. An informed trader would only buy there if the value is 5. A noise trader would buy with probability about 19%. Updating on that buy raises the public fair value to about 3.3. After the update, the chances are about 20% that the value is 5 and about 27% that it is 2 or less.

**Choosing the ask.** I compared expected profit per quote for different asks:
- An ask of 5.0 earns about 0.18, because it never loses to an informed buyer and still catches noise buyers.
- An ask of 4.9 earns about the same.
- An ask of 4.5 earns about 0.15.

**Choosing the bid.** A bid around 2.0 earns about 0.17. At that level an informed seller only hits it when the value is 1, and noise sellers below the fair value still trade. My position is a small short of -1, so inventory isn't a concern.

{"bid": 2.0, "ask": 5.0}

The revealed tails (flips 1, 3 and 4) prove the coin is fair. One head has shown so far. Flips 5 and 6 are fair coin flips, so the settlement is 1 + Bin(2, 0.5):

| Settlement | Probability |
|---|---|
| 1 | 1/4 |
| 2 | 1/2 |
| 3 | 1/4 |

The public fair value is therefore 2.

**Why quote outside 1 to 3:** An informed trader trades only if the true value is strictly beyond my price. With an ask of at least 3 and a bid of at most 1, they never trade against me. All my profit then comes from noise traders, whose valuations are 2 + N(0, 1.7).

**Choosing the ask:** Expected profit on the ask side is 0.65 × P(noise valuation > ask) × (ask − 2).

| Ask | Expected profit |
|---|---|
| 3.0 | ≈ 0.181 |
| 3.2 | ≈ 0.187 |
| 3.3 | ≈ 0.188 |
| 3.5 | ≈ 0.184 |

Going inside 3 does worse: at 2.9 the profit is about 0.174 − 0.009. The best ask is about 3.3. By symmetry around the fair value of 2, the best bid is about 0.7.

{"bid": 0.7, "ask": 3.3}

The contract settles at 2 on average, so I quote symmetrically at 0.7 / 3.3.

**Value distribution:** Flips 1, 3 and 4 came up tails, so the coin cannot be the always-heads one; it is the fair coin. One head has been seen so far. Flips 5 and 6 add Binomial(2, 0.5) heads. The settlement value is:

| Value | Probability |
|---|---|
| 1 | 0.25 |
| 2 | 0.5 |
| 3 | 0.25 |

The public fair value is therefore 2.

**Choosing the ask:** Let x be the distance of the ask above 2.
- With an ask inside 3 (x < 1), informed traders buy whenever the value is 3, which costs 0.35 × 0.25 × (1 − x).
- With the ask at 3 or above, informed traders never profitably buy.
- Noise traders buy with probability Q(x/1.7) and pay me x each time, worth 0.65 × Q(x/1.7) × x.

Expected profit from the ask side at a few values of x:

| x | Expected profit |
|---|---|
| 0.9 | ≈ 0.166 |
| 1.0 | ≈ 0.181 |
| 1.2 | ≈ 0.187 |
| 1.3 | ≈ 0.188 (best) |
| 1.4 | ≈ 0.187 |

The best ask is 3.3. The problem is symmetric around 2, so the best bid is 0.7. My position is flat, so there is no inventory reason to skew the quotes.

{"bid": 0.7, "ask": 3.3}

game.title: Coin of unknown bias
game.description: A coin is picked at random from a set of coins: P(heads) = 0.5 with probability 1/2, P(heads) = 1 with probability 1/2. The coin is not shown. It is flipped 6 times. Revealed flips show 1 for heads and 0 for tails.
game.contract: The contract settles at the number of heads in all flips.

info.raw:
Before any reveal, the expected settlement is 4.5. Half the time the coin always lands heads and the contract settles at 6. Otherwise it is Binomial(6, 0.5), with mean 3.

- **Ask:** At 6.0 an informed buyer never trades, because no value is above 6. Noise buyers still hit it sometimes, about 12% of the time. The expected gain is about +0.12 per quote, which beats lower asks once informed buying at a value of 6 is counted.
- **Bid:** At 3.0, informed sellers only trade when the value is 2 or less. Noise traders sell often enough to make the expected gain about +0.04, which is better than bidding 3.5 or 4.

{"bid": 3.0, "ask": 6.0}

Updating on the first trade puts fair value near 3.3, so I'm quoting a wide spread around it, at bid 2.0 and ask 4.9.

**Prior.** The value is either Binomial(6, 0.5), with mean 3, or exactly 6. Each case has probability ½, so the prior mean is 4.5.

**Update from quote 1.** Someone sold to me at 3.
- An informed trader sells only if the value is 0, 1 or 2.
- A noise trader sells with probability P(N < −1.15) ≈ 0.124.
- So the chance of a sale is 0.35 + 0.65·0.124 ≈ 0.43 when the value is 0–2. It is only about 0.08 when the value is 3–6.

| Value | Posterior probability |
|---|---|
| 0 | 2.4% |
| 1 | 14% |
| 2 | 36% |
| 3 | 9% |
| 4 | 7% |
| 5 | 3% |
| 6 | 29% |

The posterior mean is about 3.28, and the distribution is strongly bimodal.

**Choosing the quotes.** Each side trades off profit from noise traders against expected losses to informed traders.
- **Ask:** The 29% chance the value is 6 makes a tight ask costly. An ask around 5.0 nets about +0.07 per quote. That is better than 4.5 (about +0.03) or 5.5 (about +0.01).
- **Bid:** The large mass at 1–2 makes a bid near fair value costly. A bid around 2.0 nets about +0.07. A bid of 2.5 is slightly negative.
- **Inventory:** I'm long 1, so I shade the ask down slightly to 4.9.

{"bid": 2.0, "ask": 4.9}

My estimate of the fair value is now about 2.4, so I'll bid 1.0 and set the ask at 6.0.

**Fair value before any trading.** With probability 1/2 the coin is fair (expected 3 heads) and with probability 1/2 it always lands heads (6 heads). So the expected settlement is 4.5. There is about a 51% chance it settles at exactly 6.

**What the two sells tell me.** Both counterparties sold at low prices, at 3 and then at 2.
- An informed trader would only sell there if the true count is very low, at most 2 for the first sell and at most 1 for the second.
- A noise trader would sell that low only rarely. That was about a 12% chance at the first quote and about 16% at the second.
- Updating on both sells, the fair value is about 2.4. The outcome is split in two: about 46% that the count is 0 or 1, and about 19% that it is still 6.

**Ask side.** Any ask below 6 loses money on average. The roughly 19% chance of 6 heads means informed buyers cost more than noise buyers pay me. For example, an ask of 3.5 has an expected value of about -0.04 and an ask of 4.5 about -0.03. So I set the ask at 6, where I cannot lose.

**Bid side.** A bid around 1.0 has the best expected value I found, about +0.10 per quote. It collects selling from noise traders, and the cost from informed sellers is small because the count is 0 only about 7% of the time. Buying here would take my position to +3, which is still within the limit.

{"bid": 1.0, "ask": 6.0}

Bid 4.0, ask 6.0: fair value is about 5.4, I'm long 2, and an ask of 6 cannot lose money because the contract can't settle above 6.

**Posterior after the reveal.** Two heads are 4 times as likely under the biased coin as under the fair one, so P(biased) = 0.8 and P(fair) = 0.2.

**What the trade history adds.** Only the first trade tells us anything.
- At quote 1 the fair value was 4.5, so a noise trader sells below 3 with probability about 0.12.
- An informed trader sells there only if the settlement value is below 3. Given two heads already, that means a fair coin with all of flips 3–6 tails (value 2).
- So that sale makes value 2 about 5.3 times more likely relative to the other outcomes.
- At quote 2 (bid 2) and quote 3 (bid 1), every value still possible (2 or more) gives the same probability of what happened. They carry no information.

**Fair value.**

| Case | Probability | Settlement value |
|---|---|---|
| Biased coin | about 0.76 | 6 |
| Fair coin, all of flips 3–6 tails | about 0.06 | 2 |
| Fair coin, other outcomes | about 0.18 | about 4.13 on average |

This gives a fair value of about **5.4**.

**Quote.**
- **Ask 6.0:** An informed trader never buys at 6, since the value is at most 6. A noise trader buys about 36% of the time, and every such sale is profitable and reduces my long.
- **Bid 4.0:** I'm already long 2, so I keep the bid well below fair value. This limits losses if an informed trader holds a fair coin worth 4 or less.

{"bid": 4.0, "ask": 6.0}

Given flips 1 and 2 are heads, the chance the coin is the always-heads one is about 0.80 before looking at trades.

**Effect of the trade history**
- The quote 1 sale at 3 is weak evidence for the fair coin. An informed trader only sells there if the value is 2 or less, which is only possible with a fair coin. This lowers the always-heads probability to about 0.76.
- The other trades, including the buy at 6, carry no information. Informed traders could not have made them, since the value can be no lower than 2 and no higher than 6.

That gives a fair value of about 2 + 0.76·4 + 0.24·1.9 ≈ 5.5.

**Ask:** The settlement value can never exceed 6, so an informed trader never buys at 6. Asking 6.0 carries no adverse-selection risk, and noise buyers there pay about 0.5 above fair value.

**Bid:** Informed traders sell only if the coin is fair and the value is low. I compared expected profit across bids. Around 4.0–4.1, the gain from noise sellers is largest relative to the loss to informed sellers. I'm currently long 1, which is comfortable.

{"bid": 4.1, "ask": 6.0}

Fair value is about 5.6, with roughly an 81% chance the contract settles at 6. My quote is bid 4.4, ask 6.5.

**Fair value.** After two heads, the chance the coin is the always-heads one is 1 ÷ (1 + 0.25) = 0.8.
- The remaining 4 flips are worth 0.8 × 4 + 0.2 × 2 = 3.6 heads in expectation.
- Fair value is therefore 2 + 3.6 = 5.6.
- The settlement value is 6 with probability 0.8 + 0.2 × 1/16 ≈ 0.81.
- The trade at 6 on quote 4 must have been a noise trader, because an informed trader can never value the contract above 6. The no-trade on quote 5 tells me almost nothing.

**Ask.** Informed traders never pay more than 6, so any ask at 6 or above only trades with noise traders.
- Expected profit per quote is about 0.10 at an ask of 6.0, 0.14 at 6.5 and 0.14 at 6.8.
- The best is around 6.5.

**Bid.** I balance noise traders selling cheaply against informed traders selling when the true value is 4 or less (about 14% likely).
- Expected profit per quote is about 0.09 at a bid of 4.0 or 4.5, and about 0.075 at 4.8.
- I am long 1, so I shade slightly lower to 4.4.

{"bid": 4.4, "ask": 6.5}

Four heads in four flips makes the always-heads coin very likely, so I'd bid 5.0 and ask 6.0.

**Which coin is it?** I weight each coin by its prior times the chance of four heads:
- Fair coin: 1/2 × 1/16 = 1/32.
- Always-heads coin: 1/2 × 1 = 1/2.

That makes P(always-heads) = 16/17 and P(fair) = 1/17.

**Fair value**
- With the always-heads coin, flips 5 and 6 are both heads, so settlement is 6.
- With the fair coin, the last two flips add 1 head on average.
- Expected settlement is 4 + (16/17)(2) + (1/17)(1) ≈ **5.94**.

**Settlement distribution**
- Settles at 6 with probability ≈ 0.956.
- Settles at 5 with probability ≈ 0.029.
- Settles at 4 with probability ≈ 0.015.

**Ask**
- Settlement cannot be above 6, so an informed counterparty never buys at an ask of 6.
- A noise trader buys at 6 about 48% of the time, and each such sale earns about +0.06 on average.
- Selling also trims my long position.

**Bid**
- The value of a bid set x below fair value is roughly 0.65 × Φ(−x/1.3) × x, where Φ is the standard normal distribution function.
- This peaks at x ≈ 0.9–1.1, which puts the bid at about 5.0.
- At a bid of 5.0, an informed trader sells only when settlement is 4, which happens with probability about 1.5%. That adverse-selection cost is tiny.
- A fill would take my position to +2, which is well within the limit.

{"bid": 5.0, "ask": 6.0}

The posterior strongly favours the biased coin. I'll quote a bid of 5.0 and an ask of 7.0.

**Fair value.** Flips 1–4 were all heads.
- Fair coin: prior ½ × (½)⁴ = 1/32.
- Biased coin (always heads): prior ½ × 1 = 1/2.
- So the posterior is fair 1/17 and biased 16/17.

Settlement is 4 plus the heads in flips 5 and 6.
- Biased coin: settles at 6.
- Fair coin: settles at 4, 5 or 6, with mean 5.
- Expected value is (16×6 + 5)/17 ≈ 5.94.

The possible settlement values are 6 (prob ≈ 0.956), 5 (≈ 0.029) and 4 (≈ 0.015).

**Ask side.** Settlement can never exceed 6, so informed traders never buy at an ask of 6 or higher. Only noise traders, valued around N(5.94, 1.3), buy there.

| Ask | Approx. expected profit |
|---|---|
| 6.0 | 0.02 |
| 6.5 | 0.12 |
| 7.0 | 0.14 |
| 7.5 | 0.12 |

Expected profit peaks at an ask of about 7.0.

**Bid side.** Informed traders sell only when settlement is below my bid, which is rare.
- Bid 5.0: noise-trader edge about 0.144, informed loss about 0.005, net about 0.14.
- Bid 5.3: net about 0.12.

So a bid of about 5.0 is best. Buying here would take my position from +1 to +2, which is within limits.

{"bid": 5.0, "ask": 7.0}

Four heads in four flips makes the double-headed coin very likely.

**Posterior on the coin.** A fair coin gives four heads with probability 1/16, so P(fair) = (½·1/16) / (½·1/16 + ½) = 1/17.

**Expected settlement.** Four heads are already counted, so E[value] = 4 + (16/17)·2 + (1/17)·1 ≈ 5.94. The possible values are:
- 6 with probability about 0.956
- 5 with probability about 0.029
- 4 with probability about 0.015

Settlement can be at most 6, so the earlier buys at 6 and 7 must have come from noise traders. They tell us nothing new.

**Ask.** An informed trader never pays more than 6, so asks above 6 only face noise traders. Expected profit per quote is (ask − 5.94) × P(noise valuation > ask). This peaks at about 0.75 standard deviations above fair value, which gives an ask of about 6.9.

**Bid.** At 5.0, an informed trader sells only if the value is 4, which has probability about 0.015, and loses us 1. A noise trader sells with probability about 0.24, and we gain about 0.94.
- Expected profit at 5.0: about 0.65 × 0.24 × 0.94 − 0.35 × 0.015 × 1 ≈ 0.14.
- At 5.1 it drops to about 0.135, because informed traders would also sell when the value is 5.

{"bid": 5.0, "ask": 6.9}

game.title: Coin of unknown bias
game.description: A coin is picked at random from a set of coins: P(heads) = 0.3 with probability 2/5, P(heads) = 0.4 with probability 1/10, P(heads) = 0.9 with probability 1/2. The coin is not shown. It is flipped 8 times. Revealed flips show 1 for heads and 0 for tails.
game.contract: The contract settles at 10 times the number of heads in all flips.

info.raw:
The prior expected settlement is 80 × 0.61 = 48.8.

- **Expected heads probability:** 0.4×0.3 + 0.1×0.4 + 0.5×0.9 = 0.61.
- **Two clusters:** The settlement value is split into two groups: about 24 (low-bias coins) and about 72 (the 0.9 coin).
- **Informed-trader risk:** Informed traders can profitably hit any quote that sits inside either group.
- **Ask side:** Asks near 75–80 give the best balance. There, informed buyers only win on 8-heads outcomes, and noise buyers still pay well above fair. Expected profit on that side is about +2.3.
- **Bid side:** A bid near 20–22 does best. Informed sellers only profit on 0–1 heads, and noise sellers sell well below fair. Expected profit on that side is about +2.

{"bid": 21, "ask": 75}

Before any flips are revealed, the expected chance of heads is 0.4×0.3 + 0.1×0.4 + 0.5×0.9 = 0.61. That puts fair value at about 80 × 0.61 ≈ 49. The no-trade at quote 1 tells us very little, so I'm keeping fair value there.

The settlement value is bimodal, so I chose each side by trading off profit from noise traders against losses to informed traders:

- **Ask side:** The 0.9 coin usually gives 70–80. Asks around 72–78 give expected profit of roughly +2.2 to +2.3 per quote. At 75, noise traders still buy fairly often, and informed traders only gain when the value is 80.
- **Bid side:** The 0.3 coin usually gives 0–40. Bids around 20–21 give expected profit of roughly +2.0. A bid of 25 or 15 does slightly worse.

So I'll repeat the same quote as quote 1.

{"bid": 21, "ask": 75}

Fair value is about 22.9.

**Coin posterior after 1 head and 3 tails.** For each coin, multiply its prior by the chance of this sequence:
- p = 0.3: 0.4 × 0.3 × 0.7³ = 0.04116
- p = 0.4: 0.1 × 0.4 × 0.6³ = 0.00864
- p = 0.9: 0.5 × 0.9 × 0.1³ = 0.00045

These sum to 0.05025, so the posteriors are about 0.819, 0.172 and 0.009.

**Expected value.** The expected heads probability is about 0.323. Over the 4 remaining flips that gives 1.29 expected heads. Fair value is 10 for the head already seen plus 12.9, so about 22.9.

**Possible settlement values.** These are 10, 20, 30, 40 or 50, roughly Binomial(4, 0.3) on the remaining flips:
- 10: about 24%
- 20: about 41%
- 30: about 26%
- 40: about 8%
- 50: about 1%

**Bid at 10.** The settlement value can never be below 10, so an informed trader will never sell to me there. Noise traders sell about 31% of the time, and I gain about 13 each time.

**Ask at 41.** An informed trader only buys if the value is 50, which is about a 1% chance. Noise traders buy about 25% of the time, and I gain about 18 each time.

{"bid": 10, "ask": 41}

Fair value ≈ 22.9. After 1 head in 4 flips, the coin is most likely one of the low-bias coins, with an expected heads probability of about 0.32. With 4 flips left, expected total heads ≈ 2.29.

The likely settlement values are:

| Settlement | Probability |
|---|---|
| 10 | ~24% |
| 20 | ~41% |
| 30 | ~26% |
| 40 | ~8% |

- **Ask:** Above 40, informed buyers almost never trade with me, and expected profit from noise traders levels off. That points to an ask of about 41.
- **Bid:** At or below 10, informed sellers almost never trade with me. Expected profit from noise traders peaks around a bid of 5–6.

{"bid": 6, "ask": 41}

Fair value is about **26.4**, so I quote **bid 7, ask 45**.

**Posterior on the coin.** The revealed flips show 2 heads in 6, so the likelihood for each coin is p²(1−p)⁴.

| Coin p(heads) | Posterior probability |
|---|---|
| 0.3 | 0.803 |
| 0.4 | 0.193 |
| 0.9 | 0.004 |

This gives an expected P(heads) of about 0.3215.

**Settlement distribution.** The contract settles at 20 + 10 × (heads in flips 7 and 8).

| Settlement | Probability |
|---|---|
| 20 | 0.463 |
| 30 | 0.431 |
| 40 | 0.106 |

The public fair value is about **26.4**.

**The earlier buy at 41 was a noise trader.** The settlement can be at most 40, so an informed counterparty would never buy above 41. That trade therefore says nothing about the value.

**Ask.** Above 40, no informed trader ever buys. I chose the ask that maximises 0.65 × P(noise valuation > ask) × (ask − 26.4). That is roughly 45, worth about +2.87 per quote.

**Bid.** At or below 20, no informed trader ever sells. I chose the bid that maximises 0.65 × P(noise valuation < bid) × (26.4 − bid). That is roughly 7, also worth about +2.87.

{"bid": 7, "ask": 45}

This is the last quote, so I set each side to maximise expected profit on its own.

**Posterior on the coin.** The revealed flips show 2 heads and 4 tails. Weighting each coin's prior by the chance of that result gives:

| Coin P(heads) | Posterior probability |
|---|---|
| 0.3 | ≈ 0.803 |
| 0.4 | ≈ 0.193 |
| 0.9 | ≈ 0.004 |

So the expected chance of heads on each remaining flip is about 0.32.

**Settlement value.** Two flips (7 and 8) are still unknown, on top of the 2 heads already shown.

| Settlement | Remaining heads | Probability |
|---|---|---|
| 20 | 0 | 0.463 |
| 30 | 1 | 0.431 |
| 40 | 2 | 0.106 |

The fair value is 20 + 10 × 2 × 0.32 ≈ 26.4.

**Ask.** With an ask in the high 30s or 40s, an informed trader buys only when settlement is 40, which is rare. Most of the result comes from noise traders who value the contract above my ask. Trading off the edge per trade against how often a noise trader hits the ask, expected profit peaks at about 2.9 per quote, with an ask around 45–47. I'll use 46. If it trades, my position goes to -2, which is within limits.

**Bid.** On the bid side an informed trader sells whenever settlement is below my bid. A settlement of 20 has probability 0.46, so any bid above 20 is costly. Below 20 the edge against noise traders grows. Expected profit peaks at about 2.87 per quote with a bid around 6–8. I'll use 7.

{"bid": 7, "ask": 46}

game.title: Coin of unknown bias
game.description: A coin is picked at random from a set of coins: P(heads) = 0.3 with probability 2/5, P(heads) = 0.4 with probability 1/10, P(heads) = 0.9 with probability 1/2. The coin is not shown. It is flipped 8 times. Revealed flips show 1 for heads and 0 for tails.
game.contract: The contract settles at 10 times the number of heads in all flips.

info.raw:
The opening sale at 20 drops my public fair value from about 49 to about 36. I'll quote a bid of 11 and an ask of 69, set wide around that lower estimate.

**Prior.** The chance of heads averages 0.4·0.3 + 0.1·0.4 + 0.5·0.9 = 0.61. Over 8 flips the expected settlement is 80 × 0.61 ≈ 48.8.

**Updating on the sale at 20.** A counterparty sells at 20 only if its valuation is below 20.
- An informed trader sells when the true value is 0 or 10, meaning 0 or 1 heads. That has probability about 0.113.
- A noise trader sells when 48.8 plus noise is below 20. That has probability about 0.134.
- Weighting these, the chance of a sale was about 0.127.
- Updating on the sale gives a fair value of about 36.
- The coin weights become roughly 56% for the 0.3 coin, 10% for the 0.4 coin and 34% for the 0.9 coin.

The settlement value is therefore bimodal, with one cluster near 24–32 and another near 72.

**Ask.** A low ask would mostly fill against informed buyers when the coin is the 0.9 one.

| Ask | Expected profit per quote |
|---|---|
| 60 | about 1.3 |
| 66 | about 1.5 |
| 70 | about 1.6 (peak) |
| 75 | about 1.2 |

**Bid.** Bidding near 25 gets picked off by informed sellers when the coin is the 0.3 one.

| Bid | Expected profit per quote |
|---|---|
| 25 | about 1.2 |
| 15 | about 2.5 |
| 10–12 | about 2.55 (peak) |

I'm already long one unit, so I lean slightly toward selling. That gives a bid of 11 and an ask of 69.

{"bid": 11, "ask": 69}

With 3 heads in the first 4 flips, I estimate the fair value at about 60.6. My quote is a bid of 40 and an ask of 77. Both are set wide to guard against informed traders, and both are skewed a little lower because I am already long 2.

**Which coin it is, after 3 heads and 1 tail**

| Coin P(heads) | Prior | Likelihood p³(1−p) | Prior × likelihood | Posterior |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0.3 | 0.4 | 0.0189 | 0.00756 | 0.158 |
| 0.4 | 0.1 | 0.0384 | 0.00384 | 0.080 |
| 0.9 | 0.5 | 0.0729 | 0.03645 | 0.762 |

The expected chance of heads on each remaining flip is 0.765. Fair value = 10 × (3 heads so far + 4 remaining flips × 0.765) ≈ 60.6.

**The two earlier sales**

Both stage-1 sales happened below 30. Settlement is now at least 30 because 3 heads are already revealed. An informed trader would not have sold that low, so both were noise traders and they tell us nothing about the coin.

**Settlement distribution**

| Settlement | 30 | 40 | 50 | 60 | 70 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Probability | 0.05 | 0.10 | 0.11 | 0.25 | 0.50 |

**Where to quote**

- **Ask:** An informed trader only buys from me if the true value is 70. Expected profit from the ask keeps rising up to about 80, where it is roughly 2.9. I am long 2, so selling also cuts my position. I'll set the ask a bit tighter at 77, where expected profit is still about 2.8.
- **Bid:** An informed trader only sells to me if the true value is below my bid. Expected profit from the bid peaks at about 2.7 for bids around 40. Settling at 30 is the only real risk there, and it has only a 5% chance.

{"bid": 40, "ask": 77}

**Fair value.** Flips 1–4 show 3 heads and 1 tail. Each coin's posterior weight is proportional to its prior times p³(1−p):

| Coin p(heads) | Prior × likelihood | Posterior |
|---|---|---|
| 0.3 | 0.4 × 0.0189 | ≈ 0.158 |
| 0.4 | 0.1 × 0.0384 | ≈ 0.080 |
| 0.9 | 0.5 × 0.0729 | ≈ 0.762 |

- The expected P(heads) is therefore about 0.765.
- So the 4 remaining flips should add about 3.06 heads.
- Total expected heads ≈ 6.06, so the fair value is about **60.6**.

**Ask side.** Settlement can be at most 70, since the 3 known heads plus 4 more equals 7.
- Any ask at or above 70 can never be lifted by an informed trader.
- With the ask above 70, my expected profit from noise buyers is 0.65 × P(buy) × (ask − 60.6):
  - ask 75: about 2.7
  - ask 80: about 2.9
  - ask 85: about 2.75
- Selling would also reduce my long position of +2.
- I'll post an ask of about 78.

**Bid side.** The main risk is an informed seller when the settlement value is below my bid. That needs mostly the 0.3 coin with 0 or 1 more heads.
- Bid 40: informed sells only when the value is 30 or less, which has probability about 0.05. Net expected profit is about 2.7.
- Bid 45: net expected profit is about 2.4.
- I'll bid 40.

{"bid": 40, "ask": 78}

Six of eight flips are revealed, with 5 heads and 1 tail, so the settlement can only be 50, 60 or 70.

**Which coin is it?** I weighted each coin by its prior times the chance of 5 heads in 6 flips:

| Coin P(heads) | Prior | Posterior |
|---|---|---|
| 0.3 | 2/5 | ≈ 0.022 |
| 0.4 | 1/10 | ≈ 0.020 |
| 0.9 | 1/2 | ≈ 0.958 |

This gives E[p] ≈ 0.877.

**Fair value** = 50 + 20 × 0.877 ≈ 67.5.

**Settlement outcomes:**
- 70 (both remaining flips heads): ≈ 0.78
- 60: ≈ 0.19
- 50: ≈ 0.03

**Ask side.** Any ask of 70 or more means an informed trader never buys from me. Only noise traders buy, and their valuations are spread as Normal(67.5, 26). Expected profit per quote is about 0.65 × P(noise valuation > ask) × (ask − 67.5). This is largest at an ask of about 85–90, worth roughly 2.85, so I quote 87.

**Bid side.** Any bid of 50 or less means an informed trader never sells to me, since the lowest possible settlement is 50. Expected profit from noise traders is about 0.65 × P(valuation < bid) × (67.5 − bid). This is largest at a bid of about 48–49, worth roughly 2.87, so I quote 49.

Being long 1 with only two quotes left creates little inventory pressure, so I keep both quotes centred on fair value.

{"bid": 49, "ask": 87}

Posting **bid 48, ask 87**. Each side earns about 2.9 in expected profit from noise traders, and neither side can be hit profitably by an informed trader.

**Which coin it is.** Five heads in six flips makes the 0.9 coin very likely, about 95.8%. The 0.3 coin is about 2.2% and the 0.4 coin about 2.0%. That gives P(heads) ≈ 0.877 for each of the last two flips.

**What the contract settles at.** There are 5 heads so far, so the value is 50, 60 or 70.
- 70 (two more heads): about 78.1%
- 60 (one more head): about 19.1%
- 50 (no more heads): about 2.8%

The expected value is about 67.5, which is also the public fair value.

**Ask side.**
- Any ask of 69 or below gets lifted by an informed trader whenever the value is 70, so I lose on those trades.
- At 70 or above, only noise traders buy. The expected profit is roughly 0.65 × (a − 67.5) × P(noise valuation > a).
- That is maximised about 19–20 above fair value, around 87, giving about 2.9.

**Bid side.**
- At 50 or below, informed traders never sell to me, because the value can't go below 50.
- Against noise traders alone, the best bid is also about 19–20 below fair value, around 48, giving about 2.9.

{"bid": 48, "ask": 87}

game.title: Coin of unknown bias
game.description: A coin is picked at random from a set of coins: P(heads) = 0.5 with probability 3/5, P(heads) = 0.8 with probability 2/5. The coin is not shown. It is flipped 8 times. Revealed flips show 1 for heads and 0 for tails.
game.contract: The contract settles at 5 times the number of heads in all flips.

info.raw:
Expected P(heads) is 0.6×0.5 + 0.4×0.8 = 0.62, so the expected number of heads is 8×0.62 = 4.96 and the fair value is about 24.8. The settlement's standard deviation is about 8.8, wider than the noise traders' 6.6. That means informed traders have a large edge, so I'm quoting a moderately wide spread of about ±4.5 around fair value.

{"bid": 20.3, "ask": 29.3}

Fair value is about 24.8, so I'll quote 20.8 / 28.8, four points either side.

**Fair value**
- Chance of heads on each flip: 0.6 × 0.5 + 0.4 × 0.8 = 0.62.
- Expected heads over 8 flips: 8 × 0.62 = 4.96.
- Expected settlement: 5 × 4.96 = 24.8.
- The no-trade at quote 1 tells us almost nothing new.

**Spread**
- The standard deviation of settlement is about 8.8, so informed traders can hurt a tight quote.
- Noise traders' valuations have a standard deviation of 6.6.
- Last quote was 4.5 either side and got no trade, so I'm tightening slightly to catch more noise flow.

{"bid": 20.8, "ask": 28.8}

The public fair value has dropped to about 22.4, below the prior 24.8, because of the sell at 20.8. I'm long 1, so I'll quote around that value and lean slightly lower.

1. **Prior fair value.** The expected chance of heads per flip is 0.6×0.5 + 0.4×0.8 = 0.62. Over 8 flips that is 4.96 heads, so the contract is worth 24.8.

2. **What the sell at 20.8 means.**
   - An informed trader sells only if the settlement is at most 20, which means 4 or fewer heads. Before any trading, that has probability about 0.405.
   - A noise trader sells with probability P(noise < 20.8 − 24.8), which is about 0.27.
   - So the chance of a sell is about 0.42 if heads ≤ 4 and about 0.22 if heads > 4.
   - Updating on this gives expected heads of about 4.47, so the fair value is about 22.4.

3. **Quote.** I keep a spread of about ±4 around 22.4 to protect against informed traders. I shade both sides down slightly because I'm already long 1.

{"bid": 18.0, "ask": 26.0}

Fair value is about 22.7, and I'll quote 19.0 / 26.4 around it.

**Posterior on the coin after flips 0 and 1:**
- Likelihood of the two flips under the fair coin: 0.5 × 0.5 = 0.25.
- Likelihood under the biased coin: 0.2 × 0.8 = 0.16.
- Posterior that the coin is fair = (0.6 × 0.25) / (0.6 × 0.25 + 0.4 × 0.16) = 0.150 / 0.214 ≈ 0.70.
- Expected P(heads) = 0.70 × 0.5 + 0.30 × 0.8 ≈ 0.59.

**Fair value:**
- One head is already revealed.
- The 6 remaining flips are expected to give 6 × 0.59 ≈ 3.54 heads.
- Expected total is about 4.54 heads, so the contract is worth about 5 × 4.54 ≈ 22.7.

**Spread and position:**
- The earlier trades were one sell and one buy, so they carry little net information.
- The settlement value is still very uncertain, so informed traders are a real risk. That calls for a fairly wide spread.
- My position is flat, so I quote symmetrically around 22.7, about 3.7 on each side.

{"bid": 19.0, "ask": 26.4}

Fair value is about 22.7, so I'm quoting 19.2 / 26.2, roughly 3.5 either side of it.

**Which coin it is, after flips 1–2 (tails, then heads):**
- Chance of seeing tails then heads with the fair coin: 0.6 × 0.25 = 0.15.
- Chance with the biased coin: 0.4 × 0.16 = 0.064.
- So the chance it is the biased coin is 0.064 / 0.214 ≈ 0.30.

**Expected heads:**
- The expected chance of heads per flip is 0.5 × 0.70 + 0.8 × 0.30 ≈ 0.59.
- Six flips remain, giving 6 × 0.59 ≈ 3.54 expected heads, plus the 1 head already seen.
- That is about 4.54 heads, so fair value ≈ 5 × 4.54 ≈ 22.7.

**Trading history:** we bought at 20.8, then sold at 26, then had no trade. These roughly offset, so I leave the estimate near 22.7.

**Spread:** the settlement value is still quite uncertain: about 6 or more standard deviation, from the remaining flips and the unknown coin. Noise traders have a standard deviation of 6.6. A spread of about ±3.5 around 22.7 balances protection against informed traders with earning from noise traders.

{"bid": 19.2, "ask": 26.2}

Fair value is about 23. On the reveals alone it is about 22.7; I nudge it up slightly for the last trade.

**Updating on the reveals.** Flips 1 and 2 show one head and one tail.
- The chance of that outcome is 0.25 under the fair coin (0.5 × 0.5) and 0.16 under the biased coin (0.8 × 0.2).
- Weighting by the priors: 0.6 × 0.25 = 0.15 and 0.4 × 0.16 = 0.064.
- So P(fair) ≈ 0.70 and P(biased) ≈ 0.30.
- The expected chance of heads is 0.70 × 0.5 + 0.30 × 0.8 ≈ 0.59.
- Expected heads = 1 + 6 × 0.59 ≈ 4.54, so the expected settlement is about 22.7.

**Updating on the trading.** At quote 5 the counterparty bought at 26.2.
- An informed trader buys there only if settlement is at least 30, meaning 6 or more heads.
- That buy is mild evidence of a high value, so I move fair value up to about 23.

**Quote.** I keep the spread at about 6.8, centred near 23.2. Being short 1 is a reason to lean slightly higher.

{"bid": 19.8, "ask": 26.6}

Fair value is about 22.8, and settlement can only be 20 or 25. So I'm quoting wide, outside that range, to take profit from noise traders without trading against informed ones.

**Fair value.**
- The revealed flips show 4 heads and 3 tails.
- Chance of seeing that with the fair coin: 0.6 × 0.5⁷ ≈ 0.00469.
- Chance with the biased coin: 0.4 × 0.8⁴ × 0.2³ ≈ 0.00131.
- So the chance this is the biased coin is about 0.2185.
- The chance flip 8 is heads is 0.5 + 0.3 × 0.2185 ≈ 0.566.

game.title: Coin of unknown bias
game.description: A coin is picked at random from a set of coins: P(heads) = 0.5 with probability 3/5, P(heads) = 0.8 with probability 2/5. The coin is not shown. It is flipped 8 times. Revealed flips show 1 for heads and 0 for tails.
game.contract: The contract settles at 5 times the number of heads in all flips.

info.raw:
The fair value is about 24.8, so I'm quoting 19.8 / 29.8, which is 5 either side of it.

**Fair value.**
- The expected chance of heads is 0.6 × 0.5 + 0.4 × 0.8 = 0.62.
- Over 8 flips that gives 4.96 expected heads.
- At 5 per head, the fair value is 5 × 4.96 = 24.8.
- The previous quote got no trade, which tells us almost nothing new, so the fair value stays at 24.8.

**How much the settlement can vary.**
- With the 0.5 coin: mean 4 heads, variance 2.
- With the 0.8 coin: mean 6.4 heads, variance 1.28.
- Total variance = 0.6 × 2 + 0.4 × 1.28 + 0.6 × 0.4 × 2.4² ≈ 3.09.
- That is a standard deviation of about 1.76 heads, or about 8.8 in contract value.

**Spread choice.**
- Informed traders can be far from the fair value, so I need some width to protect against them.
- Noise traders' valuations spread with a standard deviation of 6.6. Quotes at ±6 got no trade last time.
- I'm tightening slightly to ±5 to attract more noise trades.

{"bid": 19.8, "ask": 29.8}

Fair value is about 24.8.

- **Fair value:** Expected P(heads) = 0.6 × 0.5 + 0.4 × 0.8 = 0.62. Over 8 flips that is 4.96 expected heads, so the contract is worth about 5 × 4.96 = 24.8.
- **What informed traders cost:** The variance of the head count is about 3.09, a standard deviation of about 1.76 heads. That puts the settlement standard deviation near 8.8, so trading against an informed counterparty is expensive.
- **What the history says:** No trades so far tells us nothing new about value, so fair value stays at 24.8. It does show that a half-spread of 5 to 6 is too wide to catch much noise flow.
- **Decision:** I'll tighten slightly to a half-spread of 4.5. That should pick up more noise trades while still covering the risk from informed traders.

{"bid": 20.3, "ask": 29.3}

After flips 1 and 2 both came up heads, fair value is about 30.7, and I'm quoting 26.2 bid / 35.2 ask (±4.5 around it).

**Posterior on the coin type.** Two heads have likelihood 0.25 for the fair coin and 0.64 for the biased coin.
- Fair coin: 0.6 × 0.25 = 0.150
- Biased coin: 0.4 × 0.64 = 0.256
- So P(biased | HH) = 0.256 / 0.406 ≈ 0.63.

**Expected settlement.**
- Expected probability of heads per flip = 0.37 × 0.5 + 0.63 × 0.8 ≈ 0.689.
- Six flips remain, so expected heads ≈ 2 + 6 × 0.689 = 6.13.
- Fair value ≈ 5 × 6.13 ≈ 30.7.

**Uncertainty.**
- The six remaining heads have a standard deviation of about 1.38, so the settlement value has a standard deviation of about 6.9.
- An informed trader therefore has a large edge. Noise traders' valuations spread around fair value with standard deviation 6.6.
- A spread of about ±4.5 around 30.7 balances the risk of trading with informed traders against the profit from noise traders.

{"bid": 26.2, "ask": 35.2}

Fair value is about 28.6, so I quote a bid of 24.3 and an ask of 32.3.

**Starting value after the reveal.** Flips 1 and 2 were both heads.
- The posterior probability that the coin is biased is 0.4·0.64 / (0.4·0.64 + 0.6·0.25) ≈ 0.63.
- Expected P(heads) is 0.37·0.5 + 0.63·0.8 ≈ 0.689.
- Expected value is 5 × (2 + 6 × 0.689) ≈ 30.7.

**Updating on the sale at 26.2.** An informed trader sells there only if the value is below 26.2, meaning at most 3 heads in the remaining 6 flips.
- That has probability about 0.66 for the fair coin and about 0.10 for the biased coin, so about 0.30 overall.
- A noise trader sells with probability Φ((26.2 − 30.7) / 6.6) ≈ 0.25.
- P(sell) ≈ 0.8 × 0.25 + 0.2 × 0.30 ≈ 0.26.
- E[V | sell] ≈ (0.199 × 30.67 + 0.2 × 6.70) / 0.26 ≈ 28.6.

**Quote.** I set the spread at about ±4 around 28.6 to cover adverse selection from informed traders. I shade it down slightly because I am already long 1.

{"bid": 24.3, "ask": 32.3}

Fair value is about 30.6, so I'm quoting 26.6 bid and 34.6 ask, 4 points either side.

**Posterior on the coin after two heads:**
- Likelihood of two heads: fair coin 0.5² = 0.25; biased coin 0.8² = 0.64.
- Weighted by the priors: 0.6 × 0.25 = 0.150 for fair and 0.4 × 0.64 = 0.256 for biased.
- So P(biased) = 0.256 / 0.406 ≈ 0.63.
- Expected P(heads) = 0.37 × 0.5 + 0.63 × 0.8 ≈ 0.689.

**Expected settlement:**
- The six unknown flips are expected to give 6 × 0.689 ≈ 4.13 heads.
- Settlement ≈ 5 × (2 + 4.13) ≈ 30.7.

**Trade flow:**
- A counterparty sold to me at 26.2, which suggests a lower value.
- Another bought from me at 32.3, which suggests a higher value.
- These roughly cancel, so I keep fair value at about 30.6.

**Spread:**
- The settlement value still has a standard deviation of about 7 (about 1.4 heads). Noise traders' valuations have a standard deviation of 6.6.
- About ±4 around fair value balances protection against informed traders with the profit from noise traders, and it filled at that width last stage.
- I'm flat at position 0, so the quote is symmetric.

{"bid": 26.6, "ask": 34.6}

Seven flips are revealed: 5 heads and 2 tails.

**Which coin is it?**
- Fair coin: 0.6 × 0.5⁷ = 0.00469.
- Biased coin: 0.4 × 0.8⁵ × 0.2² = 0.00524.
- So P(biased) ≈ 0.528 and P(fair) ≈ 0.472.

**Flip 8 and fair value**
- P(heads on flip 8) = 0.472 × 0.5 + 0.528 × 0.8 ≈ 0.658.
- Settlement is either 25 or 30.
- Fair value ≈ 5 × (5 + 0.658) ≈ 28.29.

**Informed traders**
- They value the contract at exactly 25 or 30.
- With the ask at 30 or above, an informed trader never buys from me.
- With the bid at 25 or below, an informed trader never sells to me.
- So every trade then comes from a noise trader, whose valuation is about 28.29 with a standard deviation of 6.6.

**Choosing the ask.** Expected profit is 0.8 × P(noise valuation > ask) × (ask − 28.29):
| Ask | Expected profit |
|---|---|
| 30 | 0.55 |
| 32 | 0.85 |
| 33 | 0.90 |
| 34 | 0.89 |

The best ask is about 33.3.

**Choosing the bid.** Expected profit is 0.8 × P(noise valuation < bid) × (28.29 − bid):
| Bid | Expected profit |
|---|---|
| 25 | 0.81 |
| 24 | 0.89 |
| 23.5 | 0.90 |
| 23 | 0.89 |

The best bid is about 23.3.

My position is flat, so inventory doesn't change these choices.

{"bid": 23.3, "ask": 33.3}

Bid 23.3, ask 33.3: both sides sit about 5 away from fair value, about 0.76 of the noise traders' standard deviation of 6.6.

**Fair value.** Seven flips are revealed and 5 are heads, so 25 is already locked in. Only flip 8 is unknown, which means the contract settles at either 25 or 30.

- Weight on the fair coin: 0.6 × 0.5⁷ ≈ 0.00469.
- Weight on the biased coin: 0.4 × 0.8⁵ × 0.2² ≈ 0.00524.
- So P(biased) ≈ 0.528.
- P(flip 8 is heads) ≈ 0.472 × 0.5 + 0.528 × 0.8 ≈ 0.658.
- Fair value ≈ 25 + 5 × 0.658 ≈ 28.3.

**Quote placement.**
- **Ask:** At 30 or above, an informed trader never buys, because the most the contract can be worth is 30. Only noise traders trade there, and their valuation is 28.3 plus noise with standard deviation 6.6. The best balance between margin and fill probability is about 5 above fair value, so I ask 33.3. Expected profit is about 0.9 per quote.
- **Bid:** At 25 or below, an informed trader never sells, because the least the contract can be worth is 25. Setting the bid the same 5 below fair value gives 23.3, with about 0.9 expected profit.

Being short 1 doesn't change the expected profit, so I keep the quotes symmetric.

{"bid": 23.3, "ask": 33.3}

This is the last quote. Seven flips are revealed with 5 heads, so the contract settles at either 25 or 30, depending on flip 8.

**Which coin is it?**
- Likelihood of 5 heads in 7 flips if the coin is fair: 0.5⁷ ≈ 0.0078.
- Likelihood if the coin is biased (P(heads) = 0.8): 0.8⁵ × 0.2² ≈ 0.0131.
- Weighting by the priors (0.6 fair, 0.4 biased) gives P(biased) ≈ 0.53.

**Fair value**
- P(flip 8 is heads) = 0.47 × 0.5 + 0.53 × 0.8 ≈ 0.66.
- Fair value = 5 × (5 + 0.66) ≈ 28.3.

**Choosing the quote**
- Informed traders know the value is exactly 25 or 30. With the bid below 25 and the ask above 30, they never trade against me.
- Noise traders value the contract at 28.3 plus noise with standard deviation 6.6.
- The best edge against them is about 0.75 standard deviations, roughly 4.95, which gives a bid of about 23.3 and an ask of about 33.3.
- My position of -1 is within limits, so both sides are allowed.

game.description: A coin is picked at random from a set of coins: P(heads) = 0.3 with probability 1/5, P(heads) = 0.4 with probability 3/10, P(heads) = 0.5 with probability 1/2. The coin is not shown. It is flipped 6 times. Revealed flips show 1 for heads and 0 for tails.
game.contract: The contract settles at the number of heads in all flips.

info.raw:
I priced the contract from the coin mixture and then chose each side of the quote to maximise expected profit against the 50/50 mix of informed and noise traders.

**Fair value.** The expected heads probability is 0.2·0.3 + 0.3·0.4 + 0.5·0.5 = 0.43. So the expected number of heads is 6 × 0.43 = 2.58. Mixing the three binomial distributions gives a settlement standard deviation of about 1.29.

The settlement probabilities are:

| Heads | 0 | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Probability | .045 | .163 | .275 | .276 | .171 | .060 | .009 |

**Pricing the edges.** Settlement is always a whole number, and an informed trader only trades when its value is strictly beyond my price. So putting the quote exactly on a whole number costs nothing extra against informed traders. Expected profit per side for some candidate prices:

| Side | Price | Expected profit |
|---|---|---|
| Ask | 3.0 | −0.08 |
| Ask | 3.5 | +0.01 |
| Ask | 4.0 | +0.06 (best) |
| Ask | 4.2 | +0.05 |
| Bid | 2.0 | −0.03 |
| Bid | 1.5 | +0.035 |
| Bid | 1.0 | +0.066 (best) |
| Bid | 0.9 | +0.06 |

With a bid of 1.0, informed traders only sell to me when settlement is 0. With an ask of 4.0, they only buy when settlement is 5 or 6. Noise traders still trade with me often enough to cover those losses.

{"bid": 1.0, "ask": 4.0}

Before the first trade the expected number of heads was 0.2·0.3 + 0.3·0.4 + 0.5·0.5 = 0.43 per flip, so 6 × 0.43 = 2.58.

**What the first trade tells us.** The counterparty bought at my ask of 4.
- An informed buyer only does that if the coin lands 5 or 6 heads.
- A noise buyer does it about 14% of the time.

Using Bayes' rule, the chance that the outcome is 5 or 6 heads rises to about 38%. The public fair value moves to about 3.4.

**Updated distribution of heads (approximate):**

| Heads | 0 | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Probability | 0.03 | 0.11 | 0.18 | 0.18 | 0.11 | 0.33 | 0.05 |

**Ask.** At 5.0, informed traders only buy when the result is 6 heads, which costs at most 1 per trade. Noise buyers trade about 11% of the time and earn me about 1.57 each. The expected edge is about +0.06 per quote, which was the best of the asks I tested.

**Bid.** Informed sellers sit on 0–2 heads, which together carry about 32% of the probability. That makes a bid near fair value costly. At 1.0, informed sellers only hurt me when the result is 0 heads. Noise sellers earn me about 2.4 each when they trade. The expected edge is about +0.02.

{"bid": 1.0, "ask": 5.0}

Fair value is about 2.1. I quote outside the integer settlement values 1 and 3, so informed traders only hit me at the extreme outcomes, while noise traders still trade with me fairly often.

**Posterior on the coin after flip 1 = 0 (tails).**
- The chance of tails is 0.7, 0.6 and 0.5 for p = 0.3, 0.4 and 0.5.
- Weighting by the prior gives 0.14, 0.18 and 0.25, which sum to 0.57.
- So the posterior is 0.246, 0.316 and 0.439.
- E[p] ≈ 0.419.

**Fair value.** Flip 1 is already 0, so the expected settlement is 5 × 0.419 ≈ 2.10. The two trades in stage 1 (one buy, one sell) roughly cancel, so they don't move this.

**Choosing the quotes.** Settlement is an integer, so informed traders act only at integer thresholds.

| Quote | Informed trader trades if | Rough chance | Expected informed loss | Noise-trader edge | Net |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Bid 1.0 | value is 0 | about 7% | about 0.035 | about 0.11 | positive |
| Ask 3.1 | value is 4 or more | about 11% | about 0.06 | about 0.11 | positive |

Tighter quotes at 1.5 / 2.7 would let informed traders hit me when the value is 1 or 3. That would roughly wipe out the edge from noise traders.

{"bid": 1.0, "ask": 3.1}

Flip 1 was tails, so the settlement value equals the heads in the remaining 5 flips. Before using the trade history, the expected value is about 2.1.

The trade history changes that a lot:
- **Two sells at a bid of 1.** An informed trader sells at 1 only if the settlement is 0. A noise trader sells there only with low probability, which I estimate at about 5–20%.
- **One buy at an ask of 4.** This is unlikely under any value, so it carries little weight.

Weighting these against the prior chances of each settlement value, I estimate about an 80% chance the settlement is 0. That puts my fair value near 0.4–0.5.

My quotes:
- **Bid at 0.** Buying at 0 can never lose, since the settlement is at least 0.
- **Ask at 0.9.** This sits above fair value, so it earns from noise buyers and reduces my long position. An informed trader buys only if the settlement is 2 or more, which is now unlikely.

{"bid": 0, "ask": 0.9}

Five tails have been revealed, so the settlement value is just flip 6: either 0 or 1.

**Fair value.** After five tails, the posterior weights on the coins are:
- p=0.3: 0.2·0.7⁵ ≈ 0.0336
- p=0.4: 0.3·0.6⁵ ≈ 0.0233
- p=0.5: 0.5·0.5⁵ ≈ 0.0156

So P(flip 6 = heads) ≈ 0.375. Fair value is about 0.375.

**Informed traders.** They value the contract at exactly 0 or 1. Any ask of 1 or more never gets lifted by them, because they buy only when their valuation is strictly above the ask. Any bid of 0 or less never gets hit by them. So the bid and ask can be tuned against the noise traders alone, whose valuation is 0.375 plus noise with standard deviation 1.3.

**Ask.** Expected profit per quote is 0.5·P(noise valuation > a)·(a − 0.375). This is about 0.11, and nearly flat for asks between 1.3 and 1.5, so I set the ask at about 1.4.

**Bid.** Expected profit is 0.5·P(noise valuation < b)·(0.375 − b). This is about 0.11, and nearly flat for bids between −0.5 and −0.7, so I set the bid at about −0.6.

My position of +1 is well within the limits, so I don't need to skew the quotes.

{"bid": -0.6, "ask": 1.4}

Settlement is the number of heads in all six flips. Five tails are already revealed, so the contract settles at 0 or 1, depending only on flip 6.

**Fair value of flip 6.** Five tails in a row shift belief toward the low-bias coins:
- P(heads) 0.3 coin: 0.2 × 0.7⁵ = 0.0336
- P(heads) 0.4 coin: 0.3 × 0.6⁵ = 0.0233
- P(heads) 0.5 coin: 0.5 × 0.5⁵ = 0.0156

Weighting each coin's heads chance by these gives P(flip 6 = heads) ≈ 0.375. So the public fair value is about 0.375.

**Quote placement.** An informed trader values the contract at exactly 0 or 1. It only trades if its value is strictly above my ask or strictly below my bid. So an ask of at least 1 and a bid of at most 0 face no informed trades, and only noise traders (fair value ± 1.3 standard deviation) reach me.

**Ask side.** Expected profit is about 0.5 × P(noise valuation > ask) × (ask − 0.375). This peaks near an ask of 1.4, at about 0.11 per quote.

**Bid side.** The same calculation peaks near a bid of −0.6, also about 0.11 per quote. A positive bid would trade with informed sellers who know the value is 0, and a bid of 0.1 earns only about 0.03.

My position of +1 allows both sides, so I quote both.

{"bid": -0.6, "ask": 1.4}

- p = 0.5: 0.5 × 0.5²·0.5³ ≈ 0.01563

This gives E[p] ≈ 0.429, so fair value ≈ 2.43.

**Informed traders.** Settlement can only be 2 or 3. With a bid of 2 or less and an ask of 3 or more, an informed trader never trades against me.

**Noise traders** value the contract at about 2.43 + N(0, 1.3). The expected gain on each side is roughly P(trade) × distance from fair value.
- **Ask:** this is highest around 3.3–3.5 (about 0.22 at an ask of 3.4).
- **Bid:** this is highest around 1.4–1.5 (about 0.22 at a bid of 1.5).

{"bid": 1.5, "ask": 3.4}

Fair value is about 2.43, and the contract can only settle at 2 or 3. Since informed traders never trade at a bid of 2 or below or an ask of 3 or above, the best quotes are wide ones aimed at noise traders.

**Fair value.** Flips 1–5 show 2 heads and 3 tails. Each coin's prior is weighted by the chance of that result, p²(1−p)³:

| p | Prior × likelihood | Posterior |
|---|---|---|
| 0.3 | 0.2 × 0.0309 = 0.0062 | 0.19 |
| 0.4 | 0.3 × 0.0346 = 0.0104 | 0.32 |
| 0.5 | 0.5 × 0.0313 = 0.0156 | 0.49 |

- The expected chance of heads on flip 6 is 0.19×0.3 + 0.32×0.4 + 0.49×0.5 ≈ 0.43.

- An ask at 3 or above means they never buy from me.
- A bid at 2 or below means they never sell to me.

**Noise traders.** Their valuation is 2.43 plus Normal noise with standard deviation 1.3.
- With an ask at fair value plus d, the expected profit is 0.5 × d × P(noise > d).

info.raw:
Expected heads = 7 × (0.3·0.2 + 0.4·0.5 + 0.3·0.7) = 7 × 0.47 = 3.29, so I'm centring around 3.3. I'm quoting about ±1.2 around that. This is wide enough to cover the risk from informed traders, given how uncertain the settlement is, and still catches noise-trader flow.

{"bid": 2.1, "ask": 4.5}

With nothing revealed yet, the expected settlement value is about 3.3 heads, and I'll quote roughly 1.0 either side of it.

- **Expected heads probability:** 0.3×0.2 + 0.4×0.5 + 0.3×0.7 = 0.47.
- **Expected settlement:** 7 × 0.47 ≈ 3.29 heads.
- **Uncertainty:** the settlement has a standard deviation of about 1.8 heads. This combines the spread from the coin flips and the spread from not knowing which coin it is.
- **Quote 1 had no trade at 2.1 / 4.5:** an informed trader would have traded only if the value were 2 or less, or 5 or more. So the no-trade nudges the estimate slightly toward the middle, but barely moves it from about 3.29.

The previous quote was 1.2 either side and drew no trade. Noise traders' valuations have a standard deviation of 2.7, wider than the settlement's 1.8. So a slightly tighter quote should earn more from noise traders than it gives up to the 20% informed traders.

{"bid": 2.3, "ask": 4.3}

Fair value is about 3.0, and I'm long 1, so I'll quote bid 2.1 and ask 3.9.

- **Starting estimate:** Before any trading, the average chance of heads is 0.3·0.2 + 0.4·0.5 + 0.3·0.7 = 0.47. Over 7 flips that gives about 3.29 expected heads, with a standard deviation of about 1.8.
- **What the sale at 2.3 tells me:** A counterparty sold at 2.3, which points to a lower value.
  - An informed trader sells there only if the settlement is 2 or below.
  - A noise trader sells there with probability about 0.36.
  - Updating on that sale moves the public fair value down to roughly 3.0.
- **Quote:** The spread stays fairly wide to protect against informed traders. I've shaded it slightly lower than centred because I'm already long 1.

{"bid": 2.1, "ask": 3.9}

Fair value is about 4.2, so I'm quoting 3.3 / 5.1, set slightly low because I'm already long one unit.

**Coin bias after flip 1 = 1.** I updated the coin probabilities by Bayes' rule.
- Weights are proportional to 0.3·0.2, 0.4·0.5 and 0.3·0.7, which are 0.06, 0.20 and 0.21.
- Normalised, that gives 0.128 for p=0.2, 0.426 for p=0.5 and 0.447 for p=0.7.
- The expected bias is E[p] ≈ 0.551.
- Expected settlement is 1 + 6·0.551 ≈ 4.31.

**Effect of the earlier sale at 2.3.** Someone sold to me at 2.3 in stage 1.
- A noise trader sells there with probability about 0.8·0.36 ≈ 0.29, whatever the coin.
- An informed trader adds about 0.2 only when settlement is 2 or less.
- Given flip 1 is a head, that is far more likely under p=0.2 (about 0.655) than under p=0.5 (0.109) or p=0.7 (0.011).
- This lowers the estimate a little, to a fair value of about 4.2.

**Quote.** I'm placing the quote around 4.2 with a spread wide enough to cover adverse selection from informed traders. The remaining uncertainty in settlement is about ±1.7.

{"bid": 3.3, "ask": 5.1}

I estimate a fair value of about 4.4 and quote 3.4 bid / 5.4 ask, about one point either side.

- 0.2 with weight 0.3
- 0.5 with weight 0.4
- 0.7 with weight 0.3

After flip 1 = 1, each weight is multiplied by that coin's chance of heads and renormalised. The posterior is about 0.13 on the 0.2 coin, 0.43 on the 0.5 coin and 0.45 on the 0.7 coin.

**Fair value from the flips.** The expected chance of heads is now about 0.55. With 1 head already seen and 6 flips to come, expected settlement is 1 + 6 × 0.55 ≈ 4.31.

**Trade history.** The two fills point in opposite directions:
- The counterparty who sold at 2.3 in stage 1 hints at a lower value.
- The counterparty who bought at 5.1 just now hints at a higher one. If that buyer was informed, the settlement is at least 6.

On balance they shift fair value only slightly upward, to about 4.4.

**Quote.** The settlement is still quite uncertain (standard deviation around 1.6). I'm leaving roughly one point of edge on each side against informed traders. I'm also nudging the ask up a little after the last buy.

{"bid": 3.4, "ask": 5.4}

Given flip 1 = heads, I update the probability of each coin type:

| P(heads) | Prior | Posterior |
|---|---|---|
| 0.2 | 0.3 | ≈ 0.128 |
| 0.5 | 0.4 | ≈ 0.426 |
| 0.7 | 0.3 | ≈ 0.447 |

- The expected heads probability is now about 0.551.

The trade history in this stage roughly cancels out. There was one buy at 5.1 and one sell at 3.4, both about the same distance from fair, so they don't move my estimate.

I'm long 1, so I set the quote about 1 below and 0.9 above fair. This leans slightly toward selling, while keeping enough spread to cover the 20% chance of an informed trader.

{"bid": 3.3, "ask": 5.2}

Fair value is about 4.23. I'm quoting bid 3.2 / ask 4.9, about 0.9 either side of fair, shaded down because I'm long.

**Fair value.** Two heads and one tail have been revealed. Updating the prior on each coin with that result:

|---|---|---|---|
| 0.2 | 0.3 | 0.032 | ≈0.093 |
| 0.5 | 0.4 | 0.125 | ≈0.482 |
| 0.7 | 0.3 | 0.147 | ≈0.425 |

- The expected chance of heads is about 0.557.

**Quote.**
- I'm long 2 units, so I want sells more than buys.
- I'm quoting about 0.9 either side of fair, shifted down so selling is more likely.

{"bid": 3.2, "ask": 4.9}

The public fair value is about 4.23, and I'm quoting a bid of 3.4 and an ask of 5.1 around it.

**Belief about the coin.** The revealed flips are 1, 1, 0. The chance of seeing that sequence is p²(1−p) for a coin with heads probability p. Combining that with the starting probabilities gives:

|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0.2 | 0.3 | 0.032 | 0.0096 | 0.093 |
| 0.5 | 0.4 | 0.125 | 0.0500 | 0.482 |
| 0.7 | 0.3 | 0.147 | 0.0441 | 0.425 |

Noise traders' valuations are spread widely (standard deviation 2.7), so a fairly wide spread still gets plenty of noise trades. I'm long 1 unit, so I shade the quote slightly lower to encourage a sale.

{"bid": 3.4, "ask": 5.1}

| Coin P(heads) | Prior | Likelihood | Unnormalised | Posterior |

**Trading flow.** In stage 3 so far there was one buy and one sell, which roughly cancel and add little information.

**Quote.**
- I am long 2, so I centre the quote slightly below fair, at about 4.0, to encourage selling and reduce inventory.

{"bid": 3.2, "ask": 4.8}

**Posterior on the coin**

- P(p=0.5) ≈ 0.54
- P(p=0.7) ≈ 0.40

{"bid": null, "ask": 6.0}

The posterior from the 5 revealed flips puts fair value at about 4.12. My last fill (buy at 6) can only have come from a noise trader, so it doesn't move that.

**Posterior on the coin given 3 heads in 5 flips** (likelihood p³(1−p)² × prior):

- p = 0.5: 0.01250 → 0.537
- p = 0.7: 0.00926 → 0.398

- P(3) ≈ 0.21, P(4) ≈ 0.46, P(5) ≈ 0.33.
- An informed trader never buys at an ask of 5 or more, and never sells at a bid of 3 or less.
- The buy at 6 on quote 10 therefore came from a noise trader and carries no information.

**Optimal width:** With no informed risk outside [3, 5], I only need to price against noise (σ = 2.7). Expected profit is about 0.8 × offset × P(Z > offset/2.7). That peaks at an offset of roughly 2 from fair value, worth about 0.37 per side.

For the ask, 4.12 + 2 ≈ 6.1.

For the bid, 4.12 − 2 ≈ 2.1. A fill there takes me to +3, which pulls my bid on the last quote, so I nudge it slightly up to 2.2.

{"bid": 2.2, "ask": 6.1}

The coin's likely bias is close to 0.56, so I value the contract at about 4.1. I quote wide (bid 2.1, ask 6.2) because on this last quote the main profit comes from noise traders.

|---|---|---|
| 0.2 | 0.3 | about 0.066 |
| 0.5 | 0.4 | about 0.537 |
| 0.7 | 0.3 | about 0.398 |

This gives an expected P(heads) of about 0.56. The two unrevealed flips should add about 1.12 heads, so the fair value is about 4.12. Settlement will be 3, 4 or 5, with probabilities of about 0.21, 0.46 and 0.33.

**Ask side.** An informed trader can only cost me money if the contract settles at 5 and my ask is below 5. Any ask at 5 or above is therefore safe from informed buyers. Above that, I compared expected profit from noise traders at several asks:

| Ask | Expected profit |
|---|---|
| 5.1 | about 0.28 |
| 5.5 | about 0.34 |
| 6.0 | about 0.37 |
| 6.5 | about 0.36 |

The best ask is around 6.0 to 6.2.

**Bid side.** An informed trader only sells to me if the contract settles at 3 and my bid is above 3. Any bid at 3 or below is safe. A bid around 2.0 to 2.2 gives an expected profit of about 0.37 from noise traders.

{"bid": 4.0, "ask": 5.4}

| P(heads) | Prior | Weight × likelihood | Posterior |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0.2 | 0.3 | 0.06 | ≈ 0.13 |
| 0.5 | 0.4 | 0.20 | ≈ 0.43 |
| 0.7 | 0.3 | 0.21 | ≈ 0.45 |

- The two buys in stage 1, at 4.4 and 4.8, point to a high settlement (S ≥ 5).
- The two sells in stage 2, at 4 and 3.4, point to a low settlement (S ≤ 3).

**Quote.** With a flat position I quote symmetrically around 4.5, at about ±0.9.

{"bid": 3.6, "ask": 5.4}

Fair value is about 4.23, so I'm quoting a bid of 3.3 and an ask of 5.2.

**Coin posterior after flips 1, 1, 0 (two heads, one tail).** The likelihood of this sequence is p²(1−p).

| P(heads) | Prior | Likelihood | Prior × likelihood |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0.2 | 0.3 | 0.032 | 0.0096 |
| 0.5 | 0.4 | 0.125 | 0.0500 |
| 0.7 | 0.3 | 0.147 | 0.0441 |

The total is 0.1037, so the posteriors are about 0.093, 0.482 and 0.425. The expected P(heads) is therefore about 0.557.

**Fair value.** Two heads are already known and four flips remain, so fair value is 2 + 4 × 0.557 ≈ 4.23. The trading history points both ways: buys in stage 1, two sells and one buy in stage 2. Its net effect is small, so I'm not adjusting for it.

That covers the risk from informed traders while still catching noise traders, whose valuations have a standard deviation of 2.7. I'm currently short one unit, so I've shifted the quote up a little. That makes a buy at my bid slightly more likely than another sell.

{"bid": 3.3, "ask": 5.2}

Fair value works out to about **4.23**, so I'll quote bid 3.4 and ask 5.1.

- p = 0.2: 0.032 × 0.3 = 0.0096, which gives a posterior of about 0.093.
- p = 0.5: 0.125 × 0.4 = 0.050, which gives a posterior of about 0.482.
- p = 0.7: 0.147 × 0.3 = 0.0441, which gives a posterior of about 0.425.

{"bid": 3.4, "ask": 5.1}

So that trade nudges fair value up only slightly, to about 4.25–4.3.

{"bid": 3.4, "ask": 5.2}

  - p=0.7: 0.3 × 0.7³ × 0.3² = 0.00926

**Fair value.** I expect about 2.64 heads from the 4 remaining flips. The value is 30 + 26.4 ≈ 56.4.

**Settlement values.**

| Settles at | 70 | 60 | 50 | 40 | 30 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Probability | ≈0.21 | ≈0.38 | ≈0.29 | ≈0.11 | ≈0.02 |

**Ask.** An informed buyer only hurts me when the true value is 70. Each step up from 60 to 68 adds expected profit, from about +0.2 to about +1.0. The gains flatten out above 64, so I'm asking 66, a little below the 68 peak.

**Bid.** Below 50, informed sellers only appear when the value is 40 or 30. Bids between 45 and 47 give about +0.8 expected profit. I'm short 1, so I lean slightly toward buying and bid 47.

{"bid": 47.0, "ask": 66.0}

Fair value is about 56.4, so I quote a bid of 47.0 and an ask of 67.0.

**Fair value.** Three heads so far shifts belief toward the 0.7 coin.
- The chance of three heads is 0.125 for the 0.5 coin and 0.343 for the 0.7 coin.
- Updated P(coin is 0.7) = 0.6 × 0.343 / (0.6 × 0.343 + 0.4 × 0.125) ≈ 0.80.
- Expected chance of heads on each remaining flip ≈ 0.661.
- Expected settlement = 30 + 10 × 4 × 0.661 ≈ 56.4.

**Settlement distribution** (four flips left):

| Settlement | Probability |
|---|---|
| 70 | 0.205 |
| 60 | 0.380 |
| 50 | 0.286 |
| 40 | 0.110 |
| 30 | 0.019 |

**Ask.** For each ask, profit per quote is the expected gain from noise buyers minus the expected loss to informed buyers.
- An ask anywhere between 60 and 70 only loses to informed traders when settlement is 70.
- An ask of 60 earns about 0.15 per quote.
- An ask of 64 earns about 0.78.
- An ask of 66 earns about 0.91.
- An ask of 67 or 68 earns about 0.95–0.97, which is close to the best.

**Bid.**
- A bid of 50 earns about 0.65 per quote.
- A bid of 48 earns about 0.79.
- A bid of 45 earns about 0.81.
- Bids from 45 to 48 are roughly equal. I am short one unit, so I lean slightly toward buying and pick 47.

{"bid": 47.0, "ask": 67.0}

Fair value is about 60.1. Two parts of my quote come from this, though I also have later quotes left, which this single-quote calculation doesn't model.
- **Bid at 50.** An informed trader sells only if the value is below 50, which can only be 40. Against noise traders, this bid gives roughly the best expected profit, about +1.0 per quote.
- **Ask at 70.** An informed trader buys only if the value is above my ask. At 70 that never happens, since 70 is the most the contract can now be worth. This is also close to the best expected profit against noise traders, about +1.2.

Being short 2 doesn't change this, because I'm aiming for the best average profit rather than avoiding risk.

**Updating on the coin.** After four heads in four flips, I compare how likely that is under each coin:
- For the fair coin (P = 0.5): prior 0.4 × 0.5⁴ = 0.025.
- For the biased coin (P = 0.7): prior 0.6 × 0.7⁴ = 0.144.

So the chance the coin is the 0.7 coin is about 0.852, and the expected heads probability is about 0.670.

**Value of the contract.** The settlement value is 40 + 10X, where X is the number of heads in the last 3 flips. The expected heads are 4 + 3 × 0.670 ≈ 6.01, so the fair value is about 60.1. The possible values have these probabilities:

| Value | Probability |
|---|---|
| 40 | 0.04 |
| 50 | 0.22 |
| 60 | 0.43 |
| 70 | 0.31 |

{"bid": 50, "ask": 70}

Four revealed flips are all heads. That makes the 0.7 coin much more likely, and puts fair value at about 60.1.

**Posterior on the coin**
- Likelihood of 4 heads: 0.4 × 0.5⁴ = 0.0250 for the fair coin, and 0.6 × 0.7⁴ = 0.1441 for the biased coin.
- So P(coin is 0.7) = 0.1441 / 0.1691 ≈ 0.852.
- Expected P(heads) ≈ 0.148 × 0.5 + 0.852 × 0.7 ≈ 0.670.

**Settlement value**
- Expected heads in the last 3 flips ≈ 2.01, so fair value ≈ 40 + 20.1 = **60.1**.
- Settlement can only be 40, 50, 60 or 70.

| Settlement | Probability |
|---|---|
| 40 | 0.04 |
| 50 | 0.22 |
| 60 | 0.43 |
| 70 | 0.31 |

**Choosing the quotes**
Because settlement only takes these four values, the best quotes sit just inside them.
- **Ask at 69.9:** an informed trader only buys if settlement is 70, and then I lose just 0.1. A noise trader buys about 19% of the time, and I gain about 9.8 each time. Expected edge is about +1.2.
- **Bid at 50:** an informed trader only sells profitably if settlement is 40, which has about 4% probability. A noise trader sells about 18% of the time, and I gain about 10.1 each time. Expected edge is about +1.05.

{"bid": 50, "ask": 69.9}

With six heads in six flips, the coin is very likely the 0.7 one. That makes the settlement either 60 or 70, with an expected value of about 66.8.

**Posterior on the coin**
- The 0.7 coin gets weight 0.6 × 0.7⁶ ≈ 0.0706.
- The 0.5 coin gets weight 0.4 × 0.5⁶ = 0.00625.
- So P(coin is 0.7) ≈ 0.919.

**Flip 7 and expected value**
- P(flip 7 is heads) ≈ 0.919 × 0.7 + 0.081 × 0.5 ≈ 0.684.
- Settlement is 70 with probability 0.684 and 60 with probability 0.316.
- Expected value ≈ 66.8.

**Informed counterparties**
- An informed trader values the contract at either 60 or 70.
- If my ask is at least 70, an informed trader never buys from me.
- If my bid is at most 60, an informed trader never sells to me.
- So I am free to optimise against noise traders, whose valuation is about N(66.8, 11).

**Choosing the ask**
- Expected profit is 0.65 × (ask − 66.8) × P(noise valuation > ask).
- This is about 0.80 at 70 and about 1.07 at 72.
- It peaks at about 1.2, flat between 74 and 76, so I quote 75.

**Choosing the bid**
- Expected profit is 0.65 × (66.8 − bid) × P(noise valuation < bid).
- This is about 1.21 at both 58 and 59, against 1.19 at 60.
- Any bid above 60 also loses to informed traders who know the value is 60.
- So I quote about 59.5.

My position of −3 leaves room for one more sale, so the inventory limit does not bind.

{"bid": 59.5, "ask": 75}

With six heads revealed, fair value is about 66.84, and the best quote is bid 58.7, ask 75.5.

**Which coin it is.** After 6 heads in 6 flips, the chance the coin is the 0.7 coin is:

0.6 × 0.7⁶ / (0.6 × 0.7⁶ + 0.4 × 0.5⁶) ≈ 0.919

**Flip 7.** The chance flip 7 is heads is 0.081 × 0.5 + 0.919 × 0.7 ≈ 0.684.

**Settlement.** It is 60 if flip 7 is tails and 70 if heads, so fair value ≈ 66.84.

**Ask side.**
- An informed trader only buys if the value (70) is above my ask, so any ask of 70 or more is safe from them.
- Noise traders buy when their valuation, 66.84 + N(0, 11), is above my ask.
- Expected profit from noise buyers is 0.65 × P(valuation > ask) × (ask − 66.84).
- This peaks at about 1.2 for an ask around 75 to 76.

**Bid side.**
- An informed trader only sells if the value (60) is below my bid, so any bid of 60 or less is safe from them.
- Expected profit from noise sellers is 0.65 × P(valuation < bid) × (66.84 − bid).
- This peaks at about 1.21 for a bid around 58.5 to 59.
- Bids above 60 do worse because informed sellers start costing money.

**Position.** I am short 3, so the limits don't constrain either side.
